name: Internal Knowledge Q&A
subSegment: any org with scattered internal documentation — engineering, HR, IT, and operations teams fielding repetitive 'where do I find X?' questions
description: Answers employee questions by retrieving from the company's own document repositories — wikis, runbooks, policy docs, HR handbooks, engineering specs, SOPs. Grounded in your own knowledge with citations. Replaces 'where can I find X?' Slack pings and reduces support load on senior engineers, HR, and ops teams. Generic by design — applies across every vertical with the right KB content.
outcomes: 30–50% reduction in time spent hunting for internal information — knowledge workers spend ~9 hours/week searching today (McKinsey; IDC ~8.8 hrs/week)
~2–4 hours/week recovered per knowledge worker on documentation searches
Citation-grounded answers — every response links to the source document
Improved onboarding velocity with always-available answers from the company's own documentation

roi.cost: $15K–45K/year — Bedrock invocations + Knowledge Base (OpenSearch Serverless ~$350/mo floor) + S3 + CloudWatch, scaling with query volume
roi.assumes: Illustrative: ~500 employees with established internal docs; knowledge workers spend ~9 hrs/week searching (McKinsey/IDC), ~2–4 hrs/week recovered at ~$55/hr loaded. Validate with your own numbers.

idealCustomer.size: Any company with 100+ employees and a meaningful corpus of internal documentation. Sweet spot is mid-market organizations (250–5000 employees) where senior staff are still answering basic doc questions but the company is too large for everyone to know everyone.
idealCustomer.volume: Internal docs spanning 1000+ pages across wikis, SharePoint, Confluence, Notion, Google Drive, or similar
idealCustomer.team: Whichever team owns internal communications, knowledge management, or developer experience
triggers: Senior staff repeatedly answering the same 'where can I find X?' questions
New-hire onboarding velocity bottlenecked on tribal knowledge
Documentation exists but no one can find it — the search bar in the wiki is a joke
Slack channels like #ask-eng or #ask-hr drowning in low-value lookups
Compliance/audit pressure to make policy documents discoverable
disqualifiers: Documentation doesn't exist (this kit retrieves; it doesn't author)
Documents are scattered across formats with no extraction pipeline (PDFs without OCR, scanned images, video-only training)
Strict information barriers required between teams (kit is single-tenant by default; multi-tenant with row-level access control is a larger build)

customerCustomizes: Source document connections (Confluence, SharePoint, Google Drive, Notion, S3, GitHub wikis, custom)
Document refresh cadence and ingestion triggers
Guardrail rules (PII redaction, off-topic refusal, escalation language)
Channel surfaces (Slack bot, web chat, internal portal embed, Teams)
preBuilt: AgentCore Managed Harness configured for retrieval-grounded Q&A
Knowledge Bases structure with chunking + embedding strategy
Guardrails template (PII redaction, off-topic refusal, citation requirement, no fabrication)
System prompt enforcing 'cite or decline' behavior
CloudWatch dashboard (queries/day, citation rate, refusal rate, latency, top documents accessed)
AGENTS.md + build-spec/ contract for a coding agent to implement
sharedResponsibility: This kit is an accelerator, not a managed service. You own the deployed harness, the document ingestion pipeline, and the data in your account. Sensitive documents stay in your S3/SharePoint/Confluence; the agent retrieves on demand and the model never sees data it isn't entitled to.
